engine.summary: Design of experiments: generates factorial, fractional factorial, screening, response-surface, Taguchi and mixture designs, analyses two-level experiments (effects, ANOVA, least squares with Type III sums of squares), fits and explores second-order response surfaces, scores multiple responses by desirability and computes the power of a factorial test.

surfaces.name: u-doe
surfaces.error_shape: Err(DoeError), whose variant names the reason and holds the values behind it.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-doe
surfaces.note: Native JS values in and out, typed in the .d.ts; an absent value in a result is null. Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields (parameter, index, min, max, got, expected, ...) as its other properties.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code.

source.catalog: code_catalog in src/wasm.rs, read off the crate's DoeError variants and the binding's own reasons; published as codes() in WebAssembly. What each code means is tabled in README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: The 2^k full factorial design for 2 to 7 factors. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The design is every combination of the two levels exactly once (2^k distinct rows) and every effect -- each non-empty product of columns -- sums to zero.
checks.reference: The definition of a two-level full factorial (Montgomery 2019, ch. 6)
checks.method: for k = 2..7 encodes each row as a bit pattern and compares the set with 0..2^k; for k <= 5 sums every column product

limits: Restates the definition; row order (Yates) is not checked.

operations.summary: A central composite design for 2 to 6 factors: face-centered, rotatable or inscribed, with n_center center runs; each row is labelled factorial, axial or center. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The cube, star and centre blocks have the defined coordinates (cube +-1 or +-1/alpha, star +-alpha on one axis, centre 0), the run count is 2^k + 2k + n_center, and the rotatable and inscribed designs satisfy Box and Hunter's moment conditions (odd moments zero, [iiii] = 3[iijj]) while the face-centred one does not.
checks.reference: Box & Hunter (1957), On the Experimental Attainment of Optimum Conditions; Box & Wilson (1951)
checks.method: for k = 2..6, n_center 1 and 3, all three alpha types, builds the moments from the rows

limits: Alpha is compared with (2^k)^(1/4) as the formula; orthogonal-blocking alphas are not offered.

operations.summary: A Box-Behnken design for 3, 4 or 5 factors with n_center center runs; each row is labelled edge or center. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: Every pair of factors takes the four sign combinations +-1 exactly once with the other factors at 0, the run count is 4*C(k,2) + n_center, and the columns are pairwise orthogonal.
checks.reference: Box & Behnken (1960), Some New Three Level Designs for the Study of Quantitative Variables
checks.method: for k = 3..5 and several centre counts, collects the (pair, sign) combinations of the edge rows

limits: k = 4 and 5 use every pair (the block structure the paper tabulates for k = 4 is not reproduced); rotatability is not claimed.

operations.summary: A Taguchi orthogonal array (L4, L8, L9, L12, L16, L18 or L27), using its first k columns. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: Each array (L4, L8, L9, L12, L16, L18, L27) at its full column count is an orthogonal array of strength two: for every pair of columns each pair of levels appears the same number of times; the levels are -1/+1 or -1/0/+1, and k columns are the leading k.
checks.reference: Taguchi (1987), System of Experimental Design; Rao (1947), Factorial experiments derivable from combinatorial arrangements of arrays
checks.method: for each array counts every level pair in every column pair

limits: The column arrangement (which column holds which interaction) is the module's, not checked against the printed tables; L12, L18 and L27 were corrected in the same release.

operations.summary: A definitive screening design for 2 to 12 factors. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The design is a fold-over with a centre run (2k+1 runs for even k, 2k+3 for odd k); every main effect is orthogonal to every other main effect and to every quadratic and two-factor-interaction column.
checks.reference: Jones & Nachtsheim (2011), A Class of Three-Level Designs for Definitive Screening in the Presence of Second-Order Effects, J. Quality Technology 43(1)
checks.method: for k = 2..12 checks the fold-over pairing, the zero pattern of the conference rows and all the inner products

limits: The conference matrices are tabulated for orders up to 12, so k stops at 12; it found that odd k had correlated main effects (corrected in the same release).

operations.summary: ANOVA of a balanced two-level experiment for the named effects: sums of squares, F tests, R^2, fitted values and residuals, a curvature test when the design has center points and pure error when design points repeat.

checks.claim: On a balanced replicated 2^3 each requested effect's sum of squares, F and p-value, the residual sum of squares and degrees of freedom, total sum of squares, R^2, adjusted R^2 and fitted values equal an ordinary least-squares fit's (Type III).
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS and anova_lm(typ=3) on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator)
checks.method: compares those quantities for a six-term model on sixteen runs with the reference's

limits: One balanced design; the centre-point curvature test and the pure-error split are not compared with a second implementation.

operations.summary: A least-squares fit of two-level data that need not be balanced (missing runs, unequal replication), with Type III sums of squares, coefficients, standard errors, t and F tests, fitted values and residuals.

checks.claim: On an unbalanced two-level design (corners left out, others replicated) the intercept, each coefficient, its standard error and t, its Type III sum of squares, F and p-value, the residual sum of squares and degrees of freedom, R^2, adjusted R^2 and the fitted values equal an ordinary least-squares fit.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS and anova_lm(typ=3) on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator)
checks.method: compares every reported quantity of a four-term model on nine runs with the reference's

limits: One design and model; aliased or rank-deficient requests, saturated models and a residual of exactly zero are covered by unit tests, not compared with the reference.

operations.summary: Taguchi signal-to-noise ratios in dB, one per run, from its replicate measurements, for a larger-is-better, smaller-is-better or nominal-is-best goal.

checks.claim: The larger-is-better, smaller-is-better and nominal-is-best ratios equal the formulas -10 log10 mean(1/y^2), -10 log10 mean(y^2) and 10 log10(mean^2 / sample variance); the nominal ratio does not change when the responses are in another unit.
checks.reference: Taguchi (1987), System of Experimental Design, the three ratios as defined, in NumPy 2.4.6
checks.method: compares the ratios of three runs of four replicates for each goal with the reference's, and the nominal ratio of the same replicates scaled by 1e-9

limits: The reference restates the published formulas; zero-variance runs (reported as 0 dB) are covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: A 2^(k-p) fractional factorial design from the standard generators (Montgomery 2019, Table 8.14), for the (k, p) combinations that table lists. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The matrix has 2^(k-p) distinct runs at +-1 with balanced, orthogonal main-effect columns; the set of column products equal to the all-ones column (the defining contrast subgroup, 2^p - 1 words) is exactly the words of the reported defining relation, the reported resolution is the shortest of them, and every generator equation holds row by row.
checks.reference: Box, Hunter & Hunter (2005), Statistics for Experimenters, 2nd ed., sec. 6.5; Montgomery (2019), table of standard fractions
checks.method: for every standard fraction enumerates the 2^k - 1 column subsets of the matrix and compares them with the printed relation

limits: Only the standard fractions (k = 4..7); the choice of generators is the published one, not checked against the table.

operations.summary: The resolution, defining relation and generators of the fraction fractional_factorial(k, p) builds, so the alias structure can be derived without a published table.

checks.claim: The matrix has 2^(k-p) distinct runs at +-1 with balanced, orthogonal main-effect columns; the set of column products equal to the all-ones column (the defining contrast subgroup, 2^p - 1 words) is exactly the words of the reported defining relation, the reported resolution is the shortest of them, and every generator equation holds row by row.
checks.reference: Box, Hunter & Hunter (2005), Statistics for Experimenters, 2nd ed., sec. 6.5; Montgomery (2019), table of standard fractions
checks.method: for every standard fraction enumerates the 2^k - 1 column subsets of the matrix and compares them with the printed relation

limits: Words and resolution are derived from the matrix; the alias structure beyond the defining relation is not enumerated.

operations.summary: Every 2^(k-p) fraction fractional_factorial can build, in ascending (k, p) order, each with its resolution, defining relation and generators.

checks.claim: The list is in ascending (k, p) order and every entry describes the matrix fractional_factorial builds for it (resolution, defining relation, generators).
checks.reference: Box, Hunter & Hunter (2005), Statistics for Experimenters, 2nd ed., sec. 6.5; Montgomery (2019), table of standard fractions
checks.method: for every standard fraction enumerates the 2^k - 1 column subsets of the matrix and compares them with the printed relation

limits: The table of fractions itself is the published set; it is not extended.

operations.summary: A Plackett-Burman screening design for 1 to 19 factors, in the smallest run count N (a multiple of 4) with N - 1 >= k. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: For every k = 1..19 the run count is the smallest of 8, 12, 16, 20 above k, the columns are +-1, balanced and pairwise orthogonal, and with k = N-1 the matrix plus the all-ones column is a Hadamard matrix (orthogonal rows too).
checks.reference: Plackett & Burman (1946), The Design of Optimum Multifactorial Experiments, Biometrika 33(4)
checks.method: for every k builds the column sums and inner products; for k = N-1 the row inner products

limits: Orthogonality only; the row order is the cyclic one of the paper and is not compared with a table.

operations.summary: The {q, m} simplex lattice design for a q-component mixture: every run's proportions are multiples of 1/m summing to 1, C(q + m - 1, m) runs. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The design is every composition of m into q non-negative integer parts divided by m: C(q+m-1, m) distinct points, each summing to 1.
checks.reference: Scheffe (1958), Experiments with Mixtures, J. Royal Statistical Society B 20
checks.method: for q = 2..8, m = 1..6 compares the rows with the integer compositions and the point count with the binomial

limits: Row order is not compared.

operations.summary: The simplex centroid design for a q-component mixture: the centroid of every non-empty subset of components, 2^q - 1 runs. Returns the coded design matrix with factor names, run and factor counts.

checks.claim: The design is the equal-share mixture of every non-empty subset of the q components: 2^q - 1 distinct points, each summing to 1.
checks.reference: Scheffe (1963), The Simplex-Centroid Design for Experiments with Mixtures, J. Royal Statistical Society B 25
checks.method: for q = 2..12 reads the support of each row and checks its shares

limits: Row order is not compared.

operations.summary: Main effects and interactions up to max_order of a two-level factorial experiment, with sums of squares, percent contribution, half-normal plot points and Lenth's pseudo standard error and margin of error.

checks.claim: On a balanced replicated 2^3 each main effect and two-factor interaction equals twice the least-squares coefficient, and its sum of squares the Type III sum of squares.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS and anova_lm(typ=3) on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator)
checks.method: compares the effect and the sum of squares of six terms with the reference's

limits: One balanced design and orders up to 2; Lenth's margin of error and the half-normal coordinates are not compared.

operations.summary: A second-order response surface fitted by ordinary least squares: intercept, linear, quadratic and two-factor interaction coefficients with their term names and R^2.

checks.claim: The second-order model's coefficients (intercept, linear, squared, interaction terms in the documented order) and R^2 equal an ordinary least-squares fit on the same model matrix.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator)
checks.method: compares the ten coefficients and R^2 of a three-factor rotatable central composite design (17 runs) with the reference's

limits: One well-conditioned coded design; a design that makes the normal equations nearly singular is covered by unit tests only.

operations.summary: Predictions of a fitted response surface at a batch of coded points, given row-major.

checks.claim: The prediction at a point is the model row times the coefficients.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator)
checks.method: compares the prediction of the fitted model at three points (one outside the factorial cube) with the reference's

limits: Predictions only; the model is the one fit_rsm fits.

performance.complexity: O(n · k^2) for n points and k factors.

operations.summary: The path of steepest ascent of a fitted response surface from the design center, in n_steps steps of step_size coded units.

checks.claim: The path's step j is j times the step size times the linear coefficients divided by the largest of them, for a model measured in any unit.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS on NumPy 2.4.6 (seeded generator); the path restates the documented formula
checks.method: compares the coded factor values of three steps with the reference's, and with the same model scaled by 1e-14

limits: The reference restates the documented direction; whether steepest ascent is the right search direction for a model is not checked.

operations.summary: Derringer-Suich desirability of observed responses: each response's desirability for its maximize, minimize or target goal, and the importance-weighted geometric mean of them.

checks.claim: The individual desirabilities of a maximize, a minimize and a target goal (each exponent, on the ramps, on the limits and outside) and the overall desirability as the importance-weighted geometric mean, zero when any response with a weight is zero, equal the Derringer-Suich formulas; a specification in small units is not read as on target.
checks.reference: Derringer and Suich (1980), the individual desirabilities and the importance-weighted geometric mean, restated in Python 3 with NumPy 2.4.6
checks.method: compares the three individual desirabilities and the overall one at six points, and a target specification in units of 1e-13, with the reference's

limits: The reference restates the published formulas; the choice of exponents and importance for a process is the caller's.

operations.summary: The candidate response vector with the highest overall desirability, or, when every candidate scores 0, the responses that no candidate brings within their limits.

checks.claim: The search returns the candidate with the largest overall desirability, with its individual desirabilities.
checks.reference: Derringer and Suich (1980), the individual desirabilities and the importance-weighted geometric mean, restated in Python 3 with NumPy 2.4.6
checks.method: compares the chosen candidate, its overall and individual desirabilities among six candidates with the reference's

limits: Finite candidate lists only; the infeasible outcome and the responses it names as unreachable are covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: The power of the two-sided t test of one effect in a 2^(k-p) factorial design with n_replicates replicates, from the noncentral t distribution with the fitted model's error degrees of freedom; reports the runs, the model terms and the error degrees of freedom used.

checks.claim: The power equals the two-sided noncentral-t power of one effect: standard error 2 sigma / sqrt(runs), runs - 1 - terms error degrees of freedom, noncentrality effect / standard error, with the run count and error degrees of freedom reported.
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1: scipy.stats.t.ppf and scipy.stats.nct.sf / nct.cdf
checks.method: compares the power, the run count and the error degrees of freedom of seven designs (full and fractional, 2 to 5 factors) with the reference's

limits: The reference restates the formula the crate documents (the standard error of an effect from the run count), so it checks the noncentral t arithmetic and the degrees of freedom, not the choice of model; powers above 1 - 1e-16 are not compared.
